title: Multiscale competency smooths the fitness landscape and lets search escape local maxima

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Multiscale competency smooths the fitness landscape and lets search escape local maxima

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The multiscale competency architecture smooths the fitness landscape by reducing phenotypic differences between genotypes, letting evolution explore mutations that would otherwise be lethal (e.g. a mutation that displaces the mouth but has another benefit survives because the mouth self-corrects), which makes search more efficient and helps it overcome local maxima.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2023, Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology › Implications of multiscale competency for the evolutionary process

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: By smoothing the fitness landscape, MCA makes the search process much more efficient, improving evolvability by enabling the search to overcome local maxima.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology”, Cellular and molecular life sciences : CMLS (2023), doi:10.1007/s00018-023-04790-z; section “Implications of multiscale competency for the evolutionary process”. Scope: Evolution of organisms with regulative development

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2023-agential-19: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.57

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The mechanism has a clean computational test and standard landscape metrics, but no specific public biological dataset spans the required genotype-to-development-to-fitness map. Thus models can resolve a restricted version only.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: In matched evolutionary simulations, vary developmental correction while mapping genotype fitness, ruggedness, neutral networks, lethal mutation survival, adaptation rate, and escape from engineered local maxima. Smoother landscapes and more frequent escape only in competent-development conditions would support the mechanism.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Landscape measures depend on genotype encoding and neighborhood definition.

Simulation efficiency does not establish importance in natural evolution.

Biological fitness landscapes are sparsely sampled.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.35
discriminating power: 0.7
analysis feasibility: 0.62
data existence: 0.48
operationalizability: 0.72

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The model was built to compare hardwired and regulative development and its outputs are public, so the efficiency and masking effects can be recomputed. That tests the mechanism inside the stated simulation, which covers only a thin analogue of regulative evolution. Organismal fitness landscapes and the hypothetical mouth correction are not in those files.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: From the saved competent and hardwired populations, compare phenotypic variance among genotypes, escapes from local fitness plateaus, and whether a deleterious local displacement is corrected before fitness is scored. Lower phenotypic differences and more escapes under competency would support smoothing and more efficient search in the model; identical landscapes would refute it there.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Smoothing by competency is not separated, in organisms, from canalization by other mechanisms.

The fitness landscape is a toy monotonic gradient, so local maxima of real development are not in the data.
